## Summary

Adds a presentation-independent deck legality/policy foundation (M3D2) as a
new sibling module, `policy/` - **not** wired into any UI in this slice.
Reproduces `gframe/deck_manager.cpp`'s real `DeckManager::CheckDeckSize`/
`CheckDeckContent`/`CheckCards` and `gframe/generic_duel.cpp`'s
`PlayerReady` sequencing exactly, read from source and cited line-by-line
in `docs/architecture/deck-legality.md`.

**This is a foundation only.** No QML/Qt changes. Nothing in `ui/` calls
this module yet - a deck built in the QML deck-builder still shows no
legality information at all. See
`docs/architecture/deck-legality.md`§0/§13 and
[ADR 0007](docs/adr/0007-deck-legality-policy-module.md).

## What's implemented

- **`LfList` + `parse_lflist()`/`load_lflist()`** (`policy/include/edopro_next/policy/lf_list.h`,
  `policy/src/lf_list.cpp`) - a from-scratch banlist parser matching
  `DeckManager::LoadLFListSingle`'s exact grammar: `!Name` sections,
  a `$whitelist` *prefix* match (not exact equality), the exact hash
  formula, and the exact quirks (a content line's literal-space parsing
  behaviour where a second space breaks the count parse; a duplicate code
  overwrites `content` but still XORs the hash twice).
- **`validate_deck()`** (`policy/include/edopro_next/policy/deck_validation.h`,
  `policy/src/deck_validation.cpp`) - the single first-error validator,
  reproducing upstream's exact precedence: deck size (Main/Extra/Side) ->
  unknown-card condition -> forbidden types -> Legend monster/spell/trap ->
  Skill count -> per-card (Main then Extra then Side): scope ->
  section-placement -> shared three-copy cap -> LFList/whitelist
  limitation.
- **Two upstream states kept deliberately distinct**: a null `LFList*`
  (skips every per-card check entirely) vs. a concrete, empty "N/A" list
  (still enforces scope/zone/copy-count) - modelled as
  `std::optional<LfList>`, not collapsed into one.
- **The `CHECK_UNOFFICIAL` magnitude quirk** (`ot > 0x3`, not a bitmask
  test) preserved exactly, not "fixed" - matching this project's practice
  of reproducing observed upstream behaviour faithfully (e.g. the
  level-magnitude wraparound in `data/src/card_database.cpp`).
- **`ValidationPolicy` has no default constructor.** Deck sizes, allowed
  scope, forbidden types, ritual placement, and the LFList to validate
  against must all be supplied explicitly - this project's UI has no
  networking/hosting session yet to derive them from, and this module must
  never author "the" rules of Yu-Gi-Oh (CLAUDE.md's "the UI must not
  implement game rules", extended to this layer).

## The one deliberate hash-semantic divergence: the LFList hash's undefined-behavior domain

Upstream's own hash expression (`gframe/deck_manager.cpp:80`) computes two
shift amounts directly from a file-supplied `count`. C++ requires each
shift amount to be in `[0, 31]` for a 32-bit operand
([expr.shift]) - solving that constraint gives `count in [-26, 4]` as the
**only** domain in which upstream's own expression is defined at all
(derived from the standard, not assumed - see
`docs/architecture/deck-legality.md`§10). Every real banlist count in
actual use (0-3) sits comfortably inside this range.

Outside it, this module fails closed: the line is rejected entirely, from
both `content` and `hash`, exactly like a syntactically malformed line -
rather than reproducing undefined behaviour or inventing a "safe" hash
formula upstream itself never defined and calling it source-equivalent.
`hashUnsafeCountDomainFailsClosed` pins the exact boundary.

## Update: two follow-up correction rounds (2 commits)

A fresh Codex review on the initial head found one real bug; a second fresh
review on the fix found two more. All three are fixed, with regression
coverage:

- **`ValidationPolicy` was a plain aggregate**, so `ValidationPolicy
  policy;` (default-initialization) left `allowed_cards` - a scalar enum
  with no in-class member initializer - genuinely **indeterminate**,
  which `validate_deck()`'s own switch over it then reads as undefined
  behavior; `ValidationPolicy{}` was safer but still silently picked the
  enum's first value and defaulted `lflist` to null. Fixed by replacing
  the aggregate with one mandatory constructor requiring every field as a
  positional argument, with no default arguments - the type is no longer
  default-constructible at all, so an omitted field is now a compile
  error.
- **`load_lflist()` used `buffer << file.rdbuf()`**, which bypasses
  `basic_istream::read()`'s own sentry/state-update machinery, so a
  genuine mid-read I/O error (e.g. `path` naming a directory on some
  platforms) could leave `file` reporting `good()` with silently
  empty/truncated data - contrary to this function's documented
  all-or-nothing contract. `data/src/ydk.cpp`'s `load_ydk()` already
  carries the fix (a sized `file.read()` loop) with its own empirical
  verification note for the identical operation; `load_lflist()` now
  reuses it. New test: `loadLflistDirectoryPathFailsCleanly`.
- **`DeckValidationError::card`'s doc comment omitted `ForbiddenType`**
  from the list of whole-deck-level error types that leave `card` at
  `None` (`TypeCount()` only reports whether any card matched, never
  which one) - corrected, with `forbiddenTypeFailsBeforeLegendAndSkillChecks`
  now asserting `card` stays `None`.

Test count at this point: 23 functions in `test_lf_list.cpp` + 26 in
`test_deck_validation.cpp` = 49, across 2 CTest targets, all passing.

## Update: third follow-up correction round (1 commit)

A fresh Codex review on the second head found one more real issue in
`load_lflist`'s neighbour, `parse_lflist`: `std::stol()` returns a `long`,
64 bits wide on LP64 platforms (most 64-bit Linux/macOS) - the parsed count
was narrowed to `int32_t` **before** `is_hash_safe_count()` ran, so an
adversarial value like `4294967296` (2^32) wrapped to `0` - a value
**inside** the documented `[-26, 4]` safe domain - silently defeating the
whole safety net for exactly the input it exists to catch. The same input
behaves differently on a platform where `long` is only 32 bits (e.g.
Windows): `std::stol()` itself throws for it there, landing in the
unrelated "malformed" branch instead - a platform-dependent outcome for
identical input.

Fixed by comparing the wide, not-yet-narrowed `std::stol()` result directly
against the safe domain - `[-26, 4]` is a strict subset of `int32_t`'s own
range, so this single check also guarantees the later narrowing cast is
safe, and no out-of-domain value is ever narrowed first. New regression:
`countValueThatWouldWrapToASafeValueIsStillRejected`.

Test count at this point: 24 functions in `test_lf_list.cpp` + 26 in
`test_deck_validation.cpp` = 50, across 2 CTest targets, all passing.

## Update: fourth follow-up correction round (1 commit)

A fresh Codex review on the third head found the **identical class of bug
just fixed for the count field, but for the code field**: `std::stoul()`
also returns a wide, platform-dependent type (`unsigned long`, 64 bits on
LP64). The parsed code was narrowed to `uint32_t` **before** being
range-checked, so an adversarial value like `4294967297` (2^32 + 1)
wrapped to code `1` - silently applying that line's restriction to an
entirely unrelated, legitimate card - while `4294967296` wrapped to code
`0` and was silently discarded as if it were the ordinary, deliberate
code-0 no-op. Both differ by platform depending on `unsigned long`'s width.

Fixed the same way: the wide `std::stoul()` result is range-checked against
`uint32_t::max()` before any narrowing, so an out-of-range code now falls
through to the same "malformed code or count" rejection as any other
unparseable line, on every platform. New regressions:
`codeValueThatWouldWrapToAnotherCardsCodeIsRejected`,
`codeValueThatWouldWrapToZeroIsRejectedNotTreatedAsANoOp`.

Test count at this point: 26 functions in `test_lf_list.cpp` + 26 in
`test_deck_validation.cpp` = 52, across 2 CTest targets, all passing.

## Update: final source-fidelity correction (1 commit)

The last two correction rounds above (the count-field and code-field
narrowing fixes) **overreached**: they rejected any wide `std::stol()`/
`std::stoul()` result outside a safe range *before* upstream's own
narrowing cast ran, instead of scoping the check to the *narrowed* value
the way this module's own authorized divergence was originally meant to.
This silently rejected lines upstream's own conversion would have accepted
- e.g. `4294967296` as a count narrows (via upstream's own
`static_cast<int32_t>`) to `0`, a value squarely inside the hash-safe
domain, so upstream would hash it normally; the interim fix rejected it
outright instead. For the code field there was never an authorized
divergence at all - a code's own narrowing carries no shift-undefined-
behavior risk, so `4294967297` narrowing to code `1` (applying this line's
restriction to a real, if unrelated, card) is upstream's own real,
faithfully-reproduced behavior, not a bug.

Corrected by restoring upstream's exact parse-then-narrow order
(`gframe/deck_manager.cpp:75-78`) for both fields, with the hash-safety
check (the one genuinely authorized divergence) now applied strictly to
the narrowed `int32_t count` - matching this project's own established
`.ydk`-codec precedent (`data/src/ydk.cpp`, `docs/architecture/deck-model.md`§2.5)
for reproducing `std::stoul`'s native-width, ABI-dependent parsing exactly
rather than normalizing it into a new cross-platform grammar. The three
tests that encoded the wrong ("reject on wide value") contract were
replaced with ABI-aware tests mirroring `data/tests/test_deck_ydk.cpp`'s
own `if constexpr(std::numeric_limits<...>::max() ...)` pattern, plus new
coverage for `-1` as a code (unsigned wraparound, not ABI-dependent) and a
value far beyond any native integer width. Docs (`deck-legality.md`,
ADR 0007) and header comments were corrected to state the divergence's
true, narrow scope, including the toolchain evidence (GCC's documented
implementation-defined narrowing under C++17, standardized under C++20)
this project actually relies on. The malformed-UTF-8 handling of LFList
section names was also audited and precisely documented as a real, narrow,
disclosed divergence from `BufferIO::DecodeUTF8` (valid UTF-8 round-trips
identically; malformed UTF-8 does not, and this module does not attempt to
reproduce upstream's own NUL-substitution/early-truncation behavior for
it).

Final test count: **29 functions in `test_lf_list.cpp` + 26 in
`test_deck_validation.cpp` = 55**, across 2 CTest targets, all passing.

## Explicit non-goals

No QML legality UI, no Qt adapters, no "collect every finding" validator
mode (deferred - see ADR 0007 Decision 2), no automatic Main/Extra
classification, no mutation/normalization of a `Deck`, no `.ydke`, no
artwork, no structured search filters or legacy sigil grammar, no
controller work, no networking/`HostInfo` integration, no upstream `.ydk`
interoperability harness, no `gframe/`/`ocgcore/` changes.

## Update: final documentation consistency cleanup (1 commit)

External review found a genuine contradiction left over from the previous
correction pass's own encoding audit: `deck-legality.md`'s LFList-grammar
summary (§9) still said `LfList::name`'s bytes were "identical either way"
to upstream's decoded `std::wstring`, contradicting `LfList::name`'s own
(already-corrected) doc comment, which documents malformed UTF-8 as a real
divergence. Fixed to state the equivalence claim applies only to
well-formed UTF-8, and to name the malformed-UTF-8 divergence explicitly.
Also corrected "the one deliberate divergence" (now too broad, since the
encoding behavior is a second, separate divergence) to "the one deliberate
hash-semantic divergence," with an explicit cross-reference between the
two. **Documentation and comment wording only** - no implementation, test,
CMake, CI, or UI file changed, verified by diff.
